body: Please provide the contents of your routes.php
I don't see any call to `$routes->extensions()` which would instruct the router to parse the `.json` extension. I am surprised if the extension does get parsed as you claim with debug turned on.
Ahem ... thank you :) That does fix it. But I'm not crazy, it DOES provide this json output without that route extension when debug is on.
I can confirm you are not crazy :smile:  I can reproduce the behavior as you describe even for up to date 3.0 branch.

I've came across this issue today and noticed that DebugKit uses json.

https://github.com/cakephp/debug_kit/blob/3.0/config/bootstrap.php#L48

DebugKit using extensions should only enable the json extension for routes connected in the plugin prefix. However, it looks like applying an extension in one scope will make it apply to other scopes as the RouteCollection maintains a list of all the extensions that could possibly be handled.  This is primarily to afford backwards compatibility for `Router::parseExtensions()`. I think separating the default/global extensions and extensions used in each scope might be a good solution to this issue.

issue.body:
Each route builder should not leak extensions into other scopes. When defining extensions in one route builder, they should not automatically be available in other scopes. What we want to avoid is a plugin like DebugKit adding `.json` extensions to all the application routes.

Refs #5089

issue.body:
I have a concern here which I think is either a bug or possible an issue with logic around .json extensions and how Table::get() returns its data.  

I have an ApiController that uses RequestHandler component and a route extension setup to return JSON with a .json extension. 

When I post json model data to the .json URL to my ApiController::edit($id) method, I follow Cake practices to first get() the Entity from the Table by id using: 
`$entity = $this->_table->get($id);`

The problem is that with the .json extension enabled, the return from Table::get(), line line 945: 
`$entity = $query->first();`

returns a JSON string, according to my logs

```
2014-11-20 01:23:34 Debug: {
    "id": "5334546a-77c4-4bdc-94ed-441f760c371d",
    "name": "Follow up on quote",
   <... etc>
}
```

Note it shows as string { ... } 

So, when I attempt to patch the data on the following line with 
`$this->_table->patchEntity($entity, $this->request->data)` 

.. the patchEntity() method fails with the error: 
`2014-11-20 00:50:32 Warning: Warning (4096): Argument 1 passed to Cake\ORM\Marshaller::merge() must implement interface Cake\Datasource\EntityInterface, string given, called in /Server/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/ORM/Marshaller.php on line 430 and defined in [/Server/vendor/cakephp/cakephp/src/ORM/Marshaller.php, line 278]`

Of course, its looking for an entity object, not a json string. 

Perhaps I am missing something? I haven't dug into the code to see if Table::get() should ALWAYS be returning an entity as an Entity object or not - regardless of route extensions - which is what I would expect, but if not the logic is a problem when patching. Otherwise, if it is supposed to return objects all the time, it's not and it might be a bug (?)
